definitions.gloss: your time; the time you can spare
definitions.explanation: The polite form of {時間|じかん}, used when the time in question belongs to the listener. Standard in business and service settings when asking someone to spare time or apologizing for taking it.

examples.japanese: お{時間|じかん}よろしいですか。
お{時間|じかん}をいただき、ありがとうございました。
examples.english: Thank you for giving me your time.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}のどこかで、{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}ほどお{時間|じかん}をいただけないでしょうか。
examples.english: Could I have about thirty minutes of your time somewhere next week?

notes:
The honorific prefix お plus {時間|じかん}. Use it only of the other person's time — for your own, say {時間|じかん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{時間|じかん}よろしいですか: do you have a moment?
- お{時間|じかん}をいただく: to take up your time
- お{時間|じかん}のあるときに: when you have time
- お{時間|じかん}を{取|と}らせてしまい{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません: I'm sorry to have taken up your time

REGISTER:
Common in customer service, sales calls, and email to clients. Among friends the plain {時間|じかん}ある? is the natural choice.
